release_note: When soft-route admission in `ve` rejects a submitted soft-norm source while it validates that source, the error now has one more member, `diagnostic`: the error carries the contract's record. When a check of the table fails, the record names the first one that fails and the message is that check's text; otherwise the message is the validator's. The table is `docs/spec/soft-norms-wire-table.md`; "first" is its order from top to bottom. With the check, the record gives the place in the input and a code. For most rejections the message is the same as before. It is a different message for these checks. 2.7a: A malformed party name that is not a string is shown as compact JSON instead of Python's value spelling. 2.8c: A malformed rank name that is not a string is shown as compact JSON instead of Python's value spelling. 3.2: An unsupported profile is named by the soft route's standard UnsupportedProfile text instead of a profile-specific later error. 4.1c: An invalid norm's field error ends after 'invalid norm fields' instead of listing the unit's keys. 6.5a: An AST node limit error gains the ResourceLimit prefix. 6.6: A precedence depth error gains the ResourceLimit prefix. 6.11: A generated soft premise limit error no longer appends the premise label. Whether a source is accepted or rejected has not changed. The public switch does not change the error's `code`. An error raised after that validation, while the norms are elaborated or the document is admitted, has no record, and its message is as before. Other ways of submitting a soft source (a document check, the rights route, English input) report as before. Before the switch, S4-pre changed the code of two kinds of rejected source, so that Python's code is the Lean route's: an otherwise valid source that lists `speech-acts@0` now has the code `SOFT_UNSUPPORTED_PROFILE` and the message `UnsupportedProfile: Unsupported profile speech-acts@0`, instead of `SOFT_INVALID_INPUT` and a message about incorrect fields; an otherwise valid source that lists `norm-defaults@0` and declares an `unspecified` default now has the code `SOFT_INVALID_INPUT` instead of `SOFT_UNSUPPORTED_PROFILE`, with the same message.
